ltx-shared-v1.description: LTX 0.9.1-era text encoder, tokenizer, VAE, and scheduler shared by the 0.9.1 single-file checkpoint. Do not use for 0.9.5+ checkpoints because their VAE/scheduler bundle changed.

ltx-shared-0.9.5.description: LTX-Video 0.9.5-specific text encoder, tokenizer, VAE, and scheduler. Standard must use this instead of the older shared bundle to avoid VAE/checkpoint mismatch artifacts.

cogvideox.license: See repository — custom CogVideoX license, verify terms before redistribution

optimization.notes: Wan uses Flow Matching architecture with novel 3D causal VAE. VAE can handle unlimited-length video encoding without losing temporal info. Enable tiling for consumer GPUs.

ui.description: Extremely efficient 1.3B lightweight model. Excellent for RTX 5060 and consumer GPUs. Generates 5-second 480P videos in ~4-5 minutes. Best balance of speed and quality.
pros: Fast generation (5s video in 4 mins on RTX 4090)
Flow Matching architecture more stable than diffusion
cons: Smaller model = less detail than 14B variants

verification.notes: Official Diffusers integration confirmed. Generation defaults based on Wan official model card. 480P is primary tested resolution with highest stability. 120 frames @ 24fps = 5s video (native Wan design).

optimization.notes: 14B model with FP8 quantization. ~4x smaller footprint than bfloat16. Forces sequential CPU offload on consumer GPUs. ZeroGPU-optimized.

ui.description: 14B model with FP8 quantization. 2-3x faster than 1.3B despite larger size. Supports image-to-video, video-to-video, and up to 20-second generation.
pros: Can generate up to 20 seconds (145 frames @ 24fps)
cons: Still requires sequential CPU offload on 8GB GPUs

verification.notes: Not yet tested end-to-end in this app. Generation defaults (steps=6, cfg=4.0) copied from official HF model card. FP8 dtype assumed from 'compatible with fp8 quantization & AoT compilation' statement.

optimization.notes: CogVideoXPipeline does not expose enable_vae_tiling() on the pipeline object directly — tiling/slicing must be called on pipe.vae. Confirmed via runtime AttributeError during integration testing.

hardware.recommended_gpu: 8GB+ consumer GPU with sequential CPU offload; 12GB+ for whole-submodule offload

ui.description: Fastest, lowest-VRAM CogVideoX variant. Good motion coherence on simple scenes; softer detail on complex/dynamic subjects.
pros: Lowest VRAM requirement in the CogVideoX family
Good motion coherence for simple scenes
cons: Struggles with complex or highly detailed subjects
6-second native output at 8fps — feels short/slow-motion if exported at a higher fps

verification.notes: Reference implementation for VMR v1. Generation defaults (steps=50, cfg_scale=6, fps=8) and vae tiling/slicing API location confirmed against official diffusers documentation and direct runtime testing. All other models in this file are UNVERIFIED placeholders — see their individual verification blocks.

optimization.notes: Assumed same tiling/slicing API quirk as cogvideox-2b (same pipeline class) — not independently confirmed.

ui.description: Higher-fidelity CogVideoX variant. Better prompt adherence than the 2B model at roughly double the VRAM cost.
pros: Better detail and prompt-following than CogVideoX-2B
cons: Roughly 2x the VRAM and download size of the 2B variant

verification.notes: Generation defaults copied from cogvideox-2b on the assumption they share training recipe conventions — NOT independently confirmed against 5B's own model card. Verify before treating as authoritative.

ui.description: Lightweight, very fast tier of LTX-Video. Good for quick previews on modest hardware.

ui.description: Standard quality LTX-Video tier — the confirmed sweet spot for 8GB consumer GPUs, tested end-to-end at under 2 minutes per generation.
pros: Fast — full generation in under 2 minutes on a RTX 5060
cons: Aggressive VAE compression can lose fine detail vs. CogVideoX/Hunyuan

verification.notes: Confirmed working end-to-end via direct runtime testing (full generation under 2 minutes on an 8GB RTX 5060). Generation defaults not cross-checked against Lightricks' official documentation — functional, not source-verified.
